scope: One actual command context per routine branch. All 57 before/after non-prose whole worlds match. The separate tests cover all 358 original routine command contexts.

routines.before:
You get people to stop and listen. One wants to know about dental care. You steer the conversation back to your beliefs.

6 new followers joined; $240.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Your pavement sermon draws 6 new followers and $240.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed has to explain that eternal life does not include dental cover.

routines.before:
You squeeze a pitch between people dodging your leaflets. One passer-by changes direction twice to avoid your explanation.

1 new follower joined; $40.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: You leave with 1 new follower and $40.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed asks why you can reveal the universe’s secrets but cannot get anyone to take a leaflet.

routines.before:
You finish your pitch to a bus queue just as the bus arrives. Everyone finds somewhere else to be.

0 new followers joined; $0.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: The bus arrives halfway through your revelation. Everyone boards. Taylor Reed keeps preaching to the timetable.

routines.before:
Your clip brings in recruits. The comments demand a longer explanation of your beliefs and a shorter explanation of your hair.

12 new followers joined; $480.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Your clip brings in 12 new followers and $480.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed wants to know why the comments have declared your hair the real miracle.

routines.before:
Your clip finds an interested audience. Most commenters still prefer arguing with one another under your invitation.

3 new followers joined; $120.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Your invitation lands 3 new followers and $120.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed is still arguing with an account called ProphetEater.

routines.before:
Your clip gets comments, arguments and an unsolicited haircut suggestion. It gets no recruits.

0 new followers joined; $0.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Nobody signs up. Taylor Reed reads you the top comment: “Is this a cult or a hostage video?”

routines.before:
Visitors sign up after your talk. One tries to finish the refreshments before their enlightenment begins.

16 new followers joined; $640.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: You finish the evening with 16 new followers and $640.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed explains that taking the entire snack tray home is not an initiation rite.

routines.before:
You get a signed form. Other visitors thank you for the refreshments with the firm politeness of people refusing a second date.

4 new followers joined; $160.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Your talk and refreshments bring in 4 new followers and $160.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed suggests testing which part works by letting you give the next talk without biscuits.

routines.before:
Visitors eat the refreshments and leave. You have persuaded them to accept snacks.

0 new followers joined; $0.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: The guests eat and leave without signing. Taylor Reed lifts the empty snack tray. “They were very committed to this bit.”

routines.before:
Your followers’ friends join. You deliver the welcome while the people who invited them look relieved that you are behaving yourself.

5 new followers joined; $200.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: The introductions bring you 5 new followers and $200.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed interrupts your welcome to promise everyone you are less intense once you have eaten.

routines.before:
A guest fills in a form. Conversations at the table become much more careful once the membership pitch starts.

1 new follower joined; $40.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: The invitations bring in 1 new follower and $40.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed has to explain that your followers were real people before they met you.

routines.before:
Your followers bring friends. The friends enjoy seeing them and decline to turn the friendship into a membership.

0 new followers joined; $0.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Nobody joins. Taylor Reed gets a hug from a guest and a firm request to keep your pitch out of their friendship.

routines.before:
Your stunt turns spectators into recruits. A bystander declines to stand any closer while taking a form.

24 new followers joined; $960.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: Your stunt attracts 24 new followers and $960.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed asks which part of the crowd cheering was meant to happen before you lost your dignity.

routines.before:
Your stunt interests would-be recruits. Most spectators leave with a photograph and a story they intend to tell at your expense.

7 new followers joined; $280.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: The spectacle wins you 7 new followers and $280.00 in joining fees. Taylor Reed suggests making the next revelation somewhere with fewer witnesses.

routines.before:
You attract cameras, spectators and no recruits. People enjoy watching you without wanting to become your responsibility.

0 new followers joined; $0.00 in joining fees reached the treasury.
routines.after: The crowd films everything and nobody joins. Taylor Reed quietly takes your name off the next sign.

routines.before: You explain dream messages. A follower shuts their eyes and calls it research.
routines.after: You explain dream messages. Taylor Reed asks why the universe needed them naked at a job interview.

routines.before: You interpret a follower’s dream. They correct you in front of everyone, then correct your interpretation of the correction.
routines.after: You interpret a dream. Taylor Reed corrects you in front of everyone, then corrects your interpretation of the correction.

routines.before: You describe a life hidden in a dream. Followers start comparing their own, talking over you to explain which alternate self had the worst marriage.
routines.after: You describe the lives hidden in dreams. Taylor Reed starts a furious debate about whether an imaginary spouse can demand an imaginary divorce.

routines.before: You describe the next version of reality. A follower makes you promise it will accept their existing membership.
routines.after: You describe the next version of reality. Taylor Reed wants to know whether they will still have to know their password.

routines.before: You explain how reality will improve. Someone asks why your microphone still sounds like that. The room wants that answered first.
routines.after: You announce an upgrade to existence. Taylor Reed asks if replacing you would be the free trial. The room laughs before you can answer.

routines.before: You promise that reality can improve. Followers shout suggestions until someone demands a version without your longer speeches.
routines.after: You promise a better version of reality. Taylor Reed demands the removal of back pain, mosquitoes and the need to wear trousers. The room gives you an impossible list.

routines.before: You explain the universe’s accounts. Your treasurer reminds the room that the rent still requires money from this universe.
routines.after: You explain what the universe owes you. Sam Reed reminds the room that the landlord still wants money from this universe.

routines.before: You discuss what the cosmos owes you. Followers ask what you owe them for sitting through this.
routines.after: You discuss what the cosmos owes you. Sam Reed asks what you owe the room for sitting through this.

routines.before: You declare that the universe owes everyone. Followers cheer and begin listing what they intend to collect. You struggle to regain the floor.
routines.after: You declare that the universe owes everyone. Sam Reed demands compensation for puberty. The room cheers while you search for a less expensive revelation.

routines.before: You discuss preparing for the end. A follower moves the discussion firmly towards lunch.
routines.after: You discuss preparing for the end. Taylor Reed asks if they should defrost anything.

routines.before: You say there is no time to waste. Someone points out how long you have been saying it.
routines.after: You say there is no time to waste. Taylor Reed points out how long you have been saying it.

routines.before: You speak about the time everyone has left. Followers draw closer and start discussing whom they want at the next meal.
routines.after: You speak about the time everyone has left. Taylor Reed names someone they want at the next meal. Others start adding names.

routines.before: You hint at a hidden truth. Followers wait through the break for you to reveal it.
routines.after: You hint at a hidden truth. Taylor Reed stays through the break, determined to catch you eventually saying it.

routines.before: You promise hidden knowledge. A follower demands one example. The pause grows long enough for others to repeat the question.
routines.after: You promise hidden knowledge. Taylor Reed demands one example. The pause grows long enough for the room to start chanting the question.

routines.before: You tell the room it holds knowledge the world lacks. Followers sit straighter and begin offering to explain things to one another.
routines.after: You declare the room chosen. Taylor Reed starts coaching everyone on how to walk past the unenlightened without looking smug. Nobody manages it.

routines.before: You ask everyone to look deep inside themselves. A follower announces that they have found hunger.
routines.after: You ask everyone to look deep inside themselves. Taylor Reed asks whether their perfect self can take over their share of the chores.

routines.before: You describe your own journey towards perfection. A follower asks how far you still have to go.
routines.after: You describe your own journey towards perfection. Taylor Reed asks how far you still have to go.

routines.before: You describe the person each follower could become. People start confiding in one another until you have to ask for their attention back.
routines.after: You describe everyone’s perfect inner self. Taylor Reed wants theirs to chair the next meeting. People start requesting introductions to their own.

routines.before: You keep the sermon short and leave room for silence. Several followers look pleased by this particular teaching.
routines.after: You leave room for silence. Taylor Reed closes their eyes, and you resist filling it with another explanation.

routines.before: You explain silence for so long that followers begin practising it while looking pointedly at you.
routines.after: You explain silence for so long that Taylor Reed raises a finger to their lips. The room joins in.

routines.before: You stop speaking and let the room listen. A hesitant follower starts talking. This time nobody interrupts them.
routines.after: You stop speaking and let the room listen. Taylor Reed starts talking about something difficult. This time nobody interrupts.

routines.before: You ask for a small miracle. A follower describes finding a parking space in enough detail to use up the sermon.
routines.after: You ask for a small miracle. Taylor Reed nominates the fact that this meeting might finish on time.

routines.before: You call everyday struggles blessings in disguise. Someone asks which blessing is meant to cover their bills.
routines.after: You call everyday struggles blessings in disguise. Taylor Reed asks which blessing is meant to cover their bills.

routines.before: You ask for stories of small miracles. Followers compete to tell theirs until you have a queue of people insisting theirs sounds least believable.
routines.after: You ask for small miracles. Taylor Reed describes a public toilet with paper, soap and a working lock. The room reacts as if the sea has parted.

routines.before:
You hear everyone’s dream. One is an elaborate account of making a sandwich. You wait for the revelation; it is the sandwich.

The event cost $80.00; voluntary contributions were $6.40.
routines.after: You spend $80.00 hearing everyone’s dreams. Jordan Ellis describes making a sandwich. You wait for the revelation; it is the sandwich. The collection brings in $6.40.

routines.before:
You keep explaining what followers’ dreams meant. They start explaining why you are wrong. The circle breaks up before you can settle it.

The event cost $80.00; voluntary contributions were $0.00.
routines.after: Your $80.00 dream circle turns on you when Jordan Ellis rejects your interpretation. You are still defending it as people leave.

routines.before:
You get the room comparing dreams until a usually silent follower has everyone listening. They start another account before you can close the circle.

The event cost $80.00; voluntary contributions were $8.00.
routines.after: At the $80.00 dream circle, Jordan Ellis reenacts a dream in which you were their pet hamster. Everyone wants the hamster’s side of the story. The collection brings in $8.00.

routines.before:
You sit through a peaceful silence, broken mainly by the chairs. Followers leave looking less exhausted.

The event cost $60.00; voluntary contributions were $6.40.
routines.after: Your $60.00 quiet gathering settles down. Jordan Ellis loses a battle with a squeaky chair and has to sit very still. Members leave voluntary contributions of $6.40.

routines.before:
You give so many instructions about silence that the gathering ends with followers rubbing their temples.

The event cost $60.00; voluntary contributions were $0.00.
routines.after: Your $60.00 silent gathering is mostly instructions about silence. Jordan Ellis puts their head in their hands. You explain that too.

routines.before:
You let the silence hold. Shoulders drop around the table. Someone starts to thank you, then thinks better of it.

The event cost $60.00; voluntary contributions were $8.00.
routines.after: You spend $60.00 bringing everyone together and let the silence hold. Jordan Ellis takes a long breath. For once, you leave the moment alone. Members leave voluntary contributions of $8.00.

routines.before:
You serve the supper. Everyone eats, and the loudest dispute concerns who gets the last helping.

The event cost $180.00; voluntary contributions were $6.40.
routines.after: You serve a $180.00 supper. Jordan Ellis gives up their seat to someone arriving late and keeps the conversation going from the doorway. The supper collection brings in $6.40.

routines.before:
You run late and short of food. Guests ask for a second helping and receive your increasingly careful apology.

The event cost $180.00; voluntary contributions were $0.00.
routines.after: The $180.00 supper runs late and short. Jordan Ellis has to tell the queue that your apology is the only thing available for seconds.

routines.before:
You get members and neighbours eating together. People linger over empty plates and ask when you are doing this again.

The event cost $180.00; voluntary contributions were $8.00.
routines.after: You spend $180.00 feeding members and neighbours. Jordan Ellis tries to clear the plates, but people keep pulling out chairs for one more conversation. The supper collection brings in $8.00.

routines.before:
You watch the sky with the group. A follower proposes a warm coat as the evening’s most convincing source of protection.

The event cost $120.00; voluntary contributions were $6.40.
routines.after: You spend $120.00 watching the sky together. Jordan Ellis proposes a warm coat as the evening’s most convincing source of protection. Followers contribute $6.40.

routines.before:
You point confidently in the wrong direction. Cold followers turn back and forth until someone asks when you intend to identify the car park.

The event cost $120.00; voluntary contributions were $0.00.
routines.after: You point confidently in the wrong direction during the $120.00 vigil. Jordan Ellis asks whether the car park is also beyond your understanding.

routines.before:
You guide followers through a clear sky. People keep pointing things out after the vigil ends and forget to ask you to explain their significance.

The event cost $120.00; voluntary contributions were $8.00.
routines.after: You bring everyone out for a $120.00 vigil. Jordan Ellis spots something and the group crowds closer, forgetting to ask you what it means. Followers contribute $8.00.

routines.before:
You show visitors the meetings and expenses. They stay curious after the refreshments run out.

The event cost $220.00; voluntary contributions were $6.40.
routines.after: You host a $220.00 open house. Jordan Ellis answers a visitor asking what happens if enlightenment does not suit them. Members contribute $6.40.

routines.before:
You welcome visitors and dodge their questions. They stop asking you and start exchanging looks with one another.

The event cost $220.00; voluntary contributions were $0.00.
routines.after: You spend $220.00 welcoming visitors, then dodge their questions. Jordan Ellis is left facing a guest who wants to know if you are always like this.

routines.before:
You let visitors look around and answer their questions. Members join in, eager to show off the place even when you are trying to finish the tour.

The event cost $220.00; voluntary contributions were $8.00.
routines.after: Visitors fill your $220.00 open house with questions. Jordan Ellis takes over the tour and starts showing off corners you had hoped to skip. Members contribute $8.00.

routines.before:
You get the gathering through its untidy moments. Followers help you finish instead of asking when they can leave.

The event cost $480.00; voluntary contributions were $6.40.
routines.after: Your $480.00 gathering survives its untidy moments. Jordan Ellis ushers you towards the microphone before you can attempt another grand entrance. The collection reaches $6.40.

routines.before:
You lose control of the arrangements. Followers queue for the gathering while being asked to help organise it. Nobody looks grateful for the opportunity.

The event cost $480.00; voluntary contributions were $0.00.
routines.after: A queue forms at the $480.00 gathering while you stand without a plan. Jordan Ellis has to ask the people waiting to come inside and help set it up.

routines.before:
You deliver the big gathering you advertised. Guests find seats, the programme holds together and followers cheer without waiting for your cue.

The event cost $480.00; voluntary contributions were $8.00.
routines.after: Your $480.00 gathering ends with Jordan Ellis leading a conga line chanting your title. You join at the back and lose all control of your own procession. The collection reaches $8.00.
